title: Grateful Dead Live at Frost Amphitheatre on 1982-10-10

ai_review.summary: A crystal‑clear soundboard capture of the legendary 10‑Oct‑1982 show with soaring Jerry solos, booming Phil bass and a string of standout performances (Looks Like Rain, Lost Sailor > Saint, Crazy Fingers, China Cat > Rider).
ai_review.review: The recording is generally praised as crisp and well‑balanced (despite a few speed anomalies in this particular rip and the unfortunate omission of the Space segment and The Wheel intro). Musically the concert is hailed as one of the high points of the 1982 “Frost” era – a fire‑filled first set and an even tighter second set packed with smoking renditions of Looks Like Rain, Lost Sailor > Saint, Crazy Fingers, China Cat > Rider, The Wheel and more. Most reviewers are ecstatic, noting tight interplay, powerful vocals and abundant “bombs” from Phil.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 60 reviews, the overwhelming majority rate 4‑5 stars and describe an electrifying performance; technical quality is repeatedly called clear with only minor issues (speed glitch, missing Space).

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, crisp mix with good instrument separation. Some listeners note a slight playback‑speed error in this version and the absence of the Space jam and The Wheel intro; otherwise no dropouts or major distortion.

show_quality.setlist_flow: High‑energy first set that builds into a seamless, almost nonstop second set; segues (Playin' Jam → Crazy Fingers, Lost Sailor → Saint) are praised as flawless.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as shredding with perfect tone, especially on Playin' Jam, Crazy Fingers and The Wheel; “lucid” and “on fire”.
band_member_comments.Phil: Repeatedly called a “bomb‑dropping” powerhouse with booming bass that drives the groove.
band_member_comments.Bob: Emotional, heartfelt vocals; notable ad‑libs on Looks Like Rain, powerful delivery on Satisfaction and other ballads.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent’s B3 organ solo on Little Red Rooster praised; solid organ fills throughout and occasional raw vocal moments.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey’s tight, driving beats keep the band locked in; no specific complaints.
